HAGUE CALLS FOR HARDER LINE ON DRUGS

Release time: Immediate Release
Released by : The Rt Hon William Hague MP
Date : Tuesday, 08 February 2000
Ref : 20000208122449

Speaking at the launch of the Conservative Party's new drugs policy document, the Rt Hon William Hague MP, Leader of the Conservative Party, said:

" The abuse of drugs is a major and increasing problem for our society. A sensible and effective strategy to crackdown on drugs must be at the heart of making progress on any attempt to raise standards in our schools and to tackle crime on our streets.

See
Chief Police Officers From One Of UK's Busiest Forces Say Drugs Laws Don't Work And Legalisation Is 'The Obvious Alternative Approach.'

That is why Ann Widdecombe, Theresa May and Andrew Lansley have joined me here this morning.
See
UK Conservatives May Support " Instant Fines " For Marijuana Possession


" With drug-pushers evident in and around our schools in every part of Britain, parents in this country are rightly terrified that their children might be next to fall victim. With drug dependency directly related to rising crime, people across the land are being burgled and mugged by those who are just after the means to pay for their drug habit.

" So this is not a time to mince words. Above all on this issue absolute clarity is required.

" The Government and its spokesmen are sending out mixed, confused and weak signals on drugs. I believe that Mo Mowlam and Keith Hellawell are simply wrong to call for a softer approach to those who use or deal in cannabis.

The evidence of a link between the use of soft drugs and hard drugs is compelling.
See
 " Those who insist on keeping the plant illegal bear a serious degree of moral responsibility for young marijuana users who do go on to use cocaine, heroin, PCP or other genuinely dangerous or addictive drugs. "
Alan Bock, of the Orange County Register On the Real Gateway

" For Ministers to imply that some laws on drugs are just not worth enforcing is to throw in the towel. It is irresponsible, shortsighted and defeatist.

" Tony Blair`s Government has clearly given up on a major part of the fight against drugs. Ministers are reduced to issuing appeals for tolerance and calling turning a blind eye to soft drugs some sort of strategy.
See
As It Becomes Clear That He Has No Political Future, The UK Drugs Tsar Rediscovers His Conscience.

" A Conservative Government will move clearly in the opposite direction. Not more tolerance of drugs, but less. Not softer policing, but tougher enforcement. Not making excuses, but locking up offenders.

" So today we are announcing major policy initiatives which would crack down hard on the drug trade.

" The small-time drug pushers who presently get lenient sentences because they are not the " Mr. Bigs " will find under our Government that leniency has run out for them.

" And those caught peddling any illegal drug near a school will have the book thrown at them.

" My promise to every parent is this - those who try to hook children on their vile products will be pursued, hunted down and punished severely.

" It is time for a stronger, firmer, harder attack on drugs than we have ever seen before. That is the common sense solution which Britain wants, and will get under the next Conservative government.
(MarijuanaNews note: Actually, that is not what Britain wants and Hague is such a loser that he will probably not even survive as party leader after the next election, much less become Prime Minister.)
See
Survey Shows UK Public Backs Treating Marijuana Possession Like a Parking Violation;
But Supports " Drug " Testing

The Shadow Secretary of State for Education, Theresa May MP, said: " The new policies being launched on drugs in schools will give School Heads the freedom to deal with drug problems in their schools and ensure that the curriculum communicates a strong 'say no to drugs' message.

" So in line with our Free Schools policies where Heads and Governors are free to manage themselves we will:

- Give Heads more freedom to implement anti-drugs policies in their schools by relieving them from pressure from central Government not to exclude pupils.

- Revise curriculum guidelines so that illegal drugs are dealt with as a subject in their own right with greater emphasis on the illegality of drugs and their harmful consequences for users, their families and the rest of society and a clear message of saying no to drugs is communicated.
(MarijuanaNews note: I suppose that the emphasis on " illegal drugs " means that " drug education " should go easy on alcohol, the drug that kills the most – both young and old – of Her Majesty’s subjects.)
- Give schools more encouragement to campaign actively against illegal drugs.

" We will also take tough action on those people who deal drugs to our children. Heads will have the freedom to stamp out drugs in their own schools. We will also campaign actively against illegal drug use in schools.

 " The clear message we are sending to children is that drugs are illegal, they are harmful so say no "
(MarijuanaNews note: How original! A failed DEAland policy, and a failed DEAland slogan make up the Conservative Party’s drugs policy.)
